title: Cohort Retention Heatmap
insights:
Insights from the Bus Ticket Booking App Cohort Analysis

The dataset contains a total of 14,952 events from 381 users, spanning from November 27, 2025, to February 22, 2026. The cohort retention matrix has been computed for up to 5 weeks, providing insights into user retention patterns.

1. BEST COHORT

The cohort with the strongest retention is Week 48 (W48), which has a W1 retention rate of 82.2%. This high retention could be attributed to several factors:

  • Seasonal travel trends during the holiday season, leading to increased bookings.
  • Potential marketing campaigns or promotions that were active during this period, encouraging users to return.

2. WORST COHORT

The cohort that drops off the fastest is Week 7 (W7), with a W1 retention of 40.0% and a W2 retention of 0.0%. This indicates a significant loss of users after their initial experience, suggesting that the app may not have met their expectations or that there were usability issues.

3. OVERALL TREND

Retention appears to be improving across successive cohorts. For instance, the W1 retention rates show an upward trend from 31.6% in Week 3 (W3) to 82.2% in Week 48 (W48). This suggests that product changes or enhancements may be positively impacting user engagement.

4. RETENTION STRATEGIES

To improve W1 retention, the following strategies are recommended:

  • Enhance User Experience: The drop in retention for Week 7 indicates potential usability issues. Conducting user testing and gathering feedback could help identify pain points and improve the onboarding process.
  • Targeted Marketing Campaigns: The success of Week 48 suggests that targeted marketing efforts can significantly boost retention. Implementing campaigns that focus on user engagement during peak travel times could help maintain or increase W1 retention rates.
